title: How And Why Not To Take Misbehavior Personally
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin lists five recurring reasons why some teachers never resolve chronic classroom management struggles: confusion from mixing incompatible methods and philosophies, laziness in wanting an easy fix rather than mastering one coherent approach, the mistaken belief their situation is uniquely unsolvable, excuse-making disguised as legitimate reasons, and an unconscious preference for drama and self-sabotage. His unifying diagnosis is that all five patterns share a common root -- an underlying fear of being personally responsible for classroom outcomes, since blaming circumstances lets a teacher off the hook. He argues explicitly against combining strategies from different systems (like SCM and PBIS), saying that mixing frameworks confuses students and undercuts the coherence each system depends on. The piece closes on a call to stop lying to oneself and instead choose responsibility, framing that choice as the actual determinant of whether classroom management improves.
points: Mixing strategies from different classroom management philosophies (e.g., SCM and PBIS) is identified as a common, self-defeating cause of confusion and misbehavior.
Teachers who want a quick, done-for-them fix rather than studying and internalizing one full approach are described as unlikely to see lasting improvement.
The belief that your specific teaching situation is unique and unsolvable is treated as a mistaken but common excuse that blocks progress.
All five recurring struggle patterns are traced back to a shared underlying fear of personal responsibility for classroom outcomes.
quotes: You need one classroom management approach. Picking and choosing what you like from different methods, books, or philosophies results in surefire failure.
They want three tips or a single video to right the ship. They want someone to hold their hand and walk them through what is clearly written on the page.
Rest assured, the conditions you’re experiencing, no matter how bad they seem, are the same as thousands of other teachers right now.
Here at SCM, we crush excuses underfoot like Goliath of Gath.
You have to throw away the deceptions and doubts, embrace the burden and responsibility, and decide: “I can do this and nothing will stop me.
